metadata.title: Identifying key features of resilient students in digital reading: Insights from a machine learning approach

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2018 microdata and constructs an analytic sample of ESCS-disadvantaged students and then labels ARS vs NRS based on digital reading performance. The manuscript does not report applying PISA sampling weights or any replicate-weight variance estimation (e.g., BRR/jackknife), and the ML pipeline is implemented in Python using scikit-learn and imbalanced-learn. Because the authors train an SVM classifier with class-weighting, SMOTETomek resampling, and kNN imputation, they do not describe any complex-survey-weighted estimation. Therefore, the results should be interpreted as predictive performance on the selected sample rather than population-representative estimates for the seven economies.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Start with PISA 2018 fifteen-year-old students from seven high-performing Asian economies (B-S-J-Z/China, Hong Kong, Macao, Taiwan, Japan, Korea, Singapore). First, screen to ESCS-disadvantaged students within each economy (bottom 25% of ESCS). Second, within these disadvantaged students, select those whose digital reading performance is in the top 25% across the seven economies to form the ARS group; the remaining disadvantaged students are labeled NRS. The dependent variable is then operationalized as a binary ARS (1) vs NRS (0) classification using the first plausible value for reading achievement (PVREAD1).

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2018 Digital reading (15-year-olds; PVREAD1; binary ARS vs NRS)
main_findings.performance_metrics: SVM (linear kernel) with SVM-RFE + 10-fold cross-validation: Accuracy=87.51%, AUC=94.86%, Recall=95.98%, Precision=83.11%, F-measure=88.63% (full 105-feature model); top-20-feature subset: Accuracy=84.35%, AUC=92.34%, Recall=91.51%, Precision=80.69%, F-measure=85.42%.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Digital reading the study leveraged metacognitive strategies (assessing credibility, summarizing, understanding & remembering), reading enjoyment, and ICT resources at home to classify academically resilient (ARS) vs non-resilient (NRS) disadvantaged students, finding that the SVM achieved high discrimination (Accuracy=87.51%, AUC=94.86%) and that personal experience/metacognition and enjoyment were the predominant features. This indicates that strengthening students’ digital reading metacognition and sustaining reading enjoyment may improve the identification and support of resilient learners in online learning environments, though the cross-sectional design and lack of causal identification mean effects cannot be interpreted as causal.

data.outcome_summary: The study analyzes PISA 2018 digital reading for 11,496 fifteen-year-olds from seven high-performing Asian economies (CHN, HKG, MAC, TWN, JPN, KOR, SGP), restricting to ESCS-disadvantaged students and then labeling ARS vs NRS using top-quartile digital reading performance (binary DV; PVREAD1). It trains an SVM classifier with a linear kernel, applies SVM-RFE to select key features from 105 contextual variables, imputes missing/invalid responses using kNN, normalizes features to [0,1], and addresses class imbalance using class-weighting plus SMOTETomek resampling. Using 10-fold cross-validation, the full-feature model reached Accuracy=87.51% and AUC=94.86% (Recall=95.98%, Precision=83.11%, F-measure=88.63%); the optimal top-20 subset yielded Accuracy=84.35% and AUC=92.34%. The paper does not report complex-survey weighting, and the authors note that cross-sectional PISA data cannot support causal claims about ICT or other features.
